title: Ferdinand the Catholic to Jerónimo de Vich, Pedrezuela 26 Oct 1515, AHN Estado 8715 N.73 (PARES 12751418)

steps.what: PARES search 'Vich cifrada' listed the ciphered letters of the Vich archive (AHN Estado 8714/8715); N.73 images fetched with the rest.

N.73 transcribed from line strips (124 lines, 3,177 tokens, 197 distinct; n73_transcription.txt) with a frequency count (n73_freq.txt): mostly three-letter code groups (sin 151, sud 97, no 93, zre 89, xed 68) and a smaller set of signs (X 171, TH 170, PHI 163, RH 151).

The 1511-12 nomenclator (vich1511) and the Charles I system of N.74 (1519; sex = papa, mod = tiene, sin = de) compared, and the N.79 'Clave de cifra' table: none fits N.73; no deciphered sibling in its key.

N.73: annealing against the esp318 Spanish 5-gram model with the lowercase groups split into letters, as whole units, and as context breaks around symbol runs (solve73.py, solve73g.py): about -2.7 to -3.5 per character, seeds disagree; no solution.
Split from vich1511 under the one-key rule (Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): N.73 is in a different system from the 1511-12 nomenclator, so it is its own entry.

Brackx (issue #94): joint annealing of a value for each sign (letter or common letter pair) and each code group (word, syllable, letter or unknown) under a Spanish 5-gram plus an encipherment-cost term n log(n/N); fixing signs only where the best runs agreed and contexts confirmed: 23 sign values agree, then all signs fixed (score -3.73 -> -3.37 per token).

Matched control: Lazarillo de Tormes (held out) enciphered the same way at the same size (3,282 tokens, 38 sign types, 158 group types); the same first step gets every sign token right and 35-44% of group tokens.

Code groups read by context in three passes: firm 40 types / 1,005 tokens (76%), tentative 29 / 177, unread 90 / 144; sin split into sin = es and sim = en (6 tokens image-checked), X given r/s/z by the model. Full reading of the 124 lines with sized holes and an English translation; CSP Spain II used as context only (no. 240 refers to this letter of the 26th).

Taken in here: v10_relabel.share on n73_reading.md 0.636 (839 words, 480 holes; tentative values as holes): decoded, not read. docs/_validate.py on the firm values (validation.tsv, tokens as transcribed, es-golden-age): pass.

Terrateig, Politica en Italia del Rey Catolico 1507-1516 (CSIC 1963): vol. I on the Internet Archive (politicaenitalia0001terr, lending only, search needs a login); vol. II, which should print the letters to Vich, not found online (Brackx).

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3048 tokens, 127 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.025 per letter; random keys -3.543 (z 8.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.5 (mean -2.524, z 27.8); annealer on the real text -2.027. Verdict: pass.
Brackx found Terrateig 1963 vol. I pp. 631-634 discussing this letter and quoting it at length from the minute (AGS Estado leg. 847 fol. 125; printed in full by Doussinague 1944 p. 520, not online).

Each of Terrateig's 15 passages aligned with the token stream (gapped, anchored on firm values) against 12 Don Quijote passages of the same length: the long quotation (1,069 letters) at 0.29 cost per letter (best control 0.98) on ll. 9-31, two short phrases also; 714 of its letters fall on already-firm values and agree except at 8 places, checked on the image. 27 groups read, 11 tentative values confirmed, seg and soo corrected, six tentative values replaced; 38 sin/sim/X tokens decided.

Four rounds applying the new values and reading remaining groups by context (three also from Ferdinand's letter to the Swiss of the same month, Terrateig p. 634); groups firm/tentative/unread 93% / 1% / 6% of tokens; the last round changed nothing.

Taken in here (we had taken in the gist before the crib update): v10_relabel.share 0.824 (1,099 words, 235 holes); _validate.py on the firm values pass (reading -2.025, shuffled refit -2.524, random keys -3.543). Still decoded, not read: look-alike readings 3.09%.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.978; polyphony 0.048; 115 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.027

outcome.method_basis: Michael Brackx recovered the sign alphabet ciphertext-only (joint annealing of sign and group values against a Spanish 5-gram, with an encipherment-cost term; no crib) and read 40 code-group types by context (issue #94, 23 Oct 2026); checked on a matched Lazarillo control and by docs/_validate.py (pass). He then found Terrateig 1963 vol. I pp. 631-634 quoting the letter from its minute, used the long quotation as a crib for ll. 9-31 (27 groups read, 11 tentative values confirmed, about 8 corrected) and four context rounds after it. The method stays key recovered from ciphertext-only (the alphabet and the first 40 groups came before the print was found); the code-group extension rests partly on external plaintext. The text is not read: 77 group tokens unread, look-alike readings 3.09% of letters.
outcome.fraction_read_source: brackx2026/n73_reading.md (gist refreshed 23 Oct 2026 after the Terrateig crib), research/reading_audit/v10_relabel.share: 1,099 words, 235 holes and doubtful words: 0.824 (ll. 9-31, the quoted stretch: 0.949).

texts.label: N.73, 26 Oct 1515
texts.summary: Ferdinand to Vich at Rome, 26 Oct 1515: he is displeased that through the Swiss's pride and folly in not waiting for his army, and the slowness of his viceroy and captain general, all of Italy is in danger, and still more at the weakness of the Pope, who is set on coming to terms with the French against the league's capitulation that no confederate may make peace or truce without the others; he does not believe the Pope will keep anything else, and Vich is to strengthen him on his behalf.
texts.note: 23 Oct 2026 (gist refreshed after the Terrateig crib): 0.824 of words read as sense (v10), 0.949 on ll. 9-31; look-alike readings 3.09% of letters, 5 letters over the 3% limit: decoded, not read (Brackx leaves the class to us).

prior.where: Ferdinand's minute of this letter (AGS Estado leg. 847 fol. 125, not digitised) printed in full by Doussinague, La política internacional de Fernando el Católico (1944) p. 520 (not seen, not online), and quoted at length by Terrateig, Política en Italia del Rey Católico (1963) vol. I pp. 631-634 (lines 9-31 of the cipher). A clear draft, not a decipherment: no key was published.

human: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
